Aug 26 Centre-Injection Heatmaps

6 h run, 0.6% agarose, nanoparticles injected into the centre gap, large magnet only. Comparisons: PEG vs COOH coating and BSA vs non-BSA agarose, each against a no-magnet control.

How to read: one panel per agarose type; rows are PEG + magnet (mean of r1–r3), the PEG control, COOH + magnet (mean of r1–r3) and the COOH control; columns step through the run. Each cell is the 10×10 mm block from above, spanning the whole block from its left edge with the magnet side at the right, so the centre injection gap sits near 5 mm. Block corners come from the four red dots on the holder, which makes the geometry unusually exact here (208/208 frames, aspect 1.06).

Scales differ between the two panels by necessity: BSA agarose is intrinsically cloudier and darker (raw darkness ~127 vs ~67 for non-BSA), so absolute brightness cannot be compared across panels. Within a panel every cell shares one scale, so magnet-vs-control and PEG-vs-COOH remain directly comparable.
Read the BSA panel with care. In BSA gel the cloudiness is strong enough to dominate the absolute-darkness map — the BSA controls look nearly as bright as the magnet arms despite having no magnet at all. The quantitative comparison below (magnet-side minus far-side) cancels that symmetric cloudiness and is the trustworthy readout for this run.

COOH out-transports PEG in both agarose types, and the gap is largest in non-BSA (31.6 vs 14.3 at 6 h). Transport plateaus after roughly 3–4 h in every arm. With n = 3 and repeat scatter of 4–20 L*, the COOH > PEG ordering is suggestive rather than established — it is consistent across all four condition pairs, which is what makes it worth following up.
